indexDescription: Free career tools: cover letter writer, resume bullet improver, mock interview practice, job offer comparison and LinkedIn headline writer.
indexIntro: Small, free tools for the parts of a job search that take the most time. The writing tools use only the facts you give them, and nothing is saved to your resume unless you copy it there.

tools.name: Cover Letter Generator
tools.title: Free Cover Letter Generator
tools.description: Paste your experience and a job description to get a tailored cover letter draft. It uses only your facts and never invents any. Free account.
tools.intro: Paste a few lines about your experience and the job advert. You get a short cover letter draft that you can edit and copy. It only uses what you wrote, so gaps are marked for you to fill in.
steps: Paste your resume text or a few lines about your experience and skills.
Paste the job description and add the job title and company if you know them.
Choose a tone, create the draft, then edit it so it sounds like you.
tools.note: The draft is written by AI from your text. Read it carefully, fix anything that is not true for you, and add real examples before you send it.

faqs.q: Does the generator make up experience?
faqs.a: No. It is told to use only the facts you paste. Where something is missing it leaves a [bracket] for you to fill in. Always read the letter and remove anything that is not true for you.

faqs.q: Do I need to upload my resume?
faqs.a: No. You paste text. Nothing is attached to your account resume and the letter is not stored after you leave the page.

faqs.q: How long is the letter?
faqs.a: About 250 to 300 words in three or four short paragraphs, which is usually enough for an application email or form.

tools.name: Resume Bullet Point Improver
tools.title: Resume Bullet Point Improver
tools.description: Turn weak resume lines into clear, action-led bullet points. It never invents numbers: it tells you what to add. Free with an account.
tools.intro: Paste up to eight lines from your resume. You get two stronger versions of each, starting with an action verb, plus a note on what real detail to add, such as a number you can prove.
steps: Paste one resume bullet per line.
Optionally add the job title you are aiming for.
Pick the version you like, replace the [brackets] with your real details and copy it.
tools.note: The tool never makes up numbers or results. A bracket such as [add the number of customers] means you should add a figure only if you really have it.

faqs.q: Will it add fake numbers to my bullets?
faqs.a: No. It is told never to invent figures, tools or results. It marks the place where a real number would help, and you decide whether you have one.

faqs.q: What makes a good resume bullet?
faqs.a: Start with an action verb, say what you did and, if you can prove it, the result: for example the time saved, the amount handled or the people helped.

faqs.q: How many bullets can I improve at once?
faqs.a: Up to eight lines at a time, to keep the answers focused.

tools.name: Mock Interview Practice
tools.title: Mock Interview Practice with Feedback
tools.description: Practise real interview questions, type your answer and get feedback against a model answer. Free with an account, no recording.
tools.intro: Pick a question from our interview question bank, type your answer, and get feedback: what worked, what is missing and a stronger version built from your own points. Then compare it with the model answer.
steps: Choose a level and topic, then pick a question.
Type your answer as you would say it in the interview.
Read the feedback, compare it with the model answer and try again.
tools.note: Feedback is written by AI and is a guide, not a score or a prediction of the result. Nothing is recorded, and your answer is not shared.

faqs.q: Is my answer saved or shown to others?
faqs.a: No. It is sent only to get feedback and is not published. If you want to share an answer with other job seekers, use the answer box on the question page instead.

faqs.q: Where do the questions come from?
faqs.a: From the interview questions on our Jobs pages, each with a model answer written by us.

faqs.q: Can this tell me if I will get the job?
faqs.a: No. It can only show how clear and complete your answer is compared with a model answer.

tools.name: Job Offer Comparison Calculator
tools.title: Job Offer Comparison Calculator
tools.description: Compare two job offers side by side: monthly take-home, yearly total, bonus, benefits, commute cost and notice period. Free with an account.
tools.intro: Enter the numbers from two offers and see them side by side: take-home pay, yearly total, benefits and the cost of getting to work. It runs in your browser, uses no AI and sends nothing anywhere.
steps: Enter the monthly take-home pay from each offer (after tax, from the offer or payslip).
Add bonus, benefits value, commute cost and anything else that changes your real income.
Read the yearly total and the other differences, then decide what matters most to you.
tools.note: This calculator does not work out tax. Use the take-home figure from the employer or your own estimate. Pay is only one part of a job, so also compare growth, hours and the people you will work with.

faqs.q: Does it calculate tax for me?
faqs.a: No. Tax rules differ by country and change often, so you enter your own take-home pay. The calculator then adds your bonus and benefits and subtracts your extra costs.

faqs.q: Is my data stored?
faqs.a: No. The sums run in your browser and nothing is sent to a server.

faqs.q: What counts as the value of benefits?
faqs.a: Only count benefits you would otherwise pay for yourself, such as health cover, meals or transport. Leave out anything you would not use.

faqs.q: Can I ask for more money after an offer?
faqs.a: Often you can ask, politely and with reasons. Many employers expect some discussion, but not all will change the offer, and rules differ by country, company and role. Decide beforehand what matters to you (pay, start date, holiday, remote days, training), ask for it once in writing, and be ready to accept the answer. This page gives a short checklist and a message you can adapt. It does not promise any result.

tools.name: LinkedIn Headline and About Generator
tools.title: LinkedIn Headline and About Writer
tools.description: Get three LinkedIn headline options and a clear About section written from your real experience. Free with an account, nothing invented.
tools.h1: LinkedIn headline and About section writer
tools.intro: Tell us what you do, your main skills and the kind of role you want. You get three headline options and a short About section in the first person, written only from the facts you give.
steps: Paste a few lines about your experience, skills and what you are looking for.
Add the target role and choose a tone.
Pick a headline, edit the About section and paste both into your LinkedIn profile.
tools.note: The text is written by AI from your facts. Check every claim before you post it, and remove anything that is not true for you.

faqs.q: How long can a LinkedIn headline be?
faqs.a: LinkedIn allows up to 220 characters for the headline. The options we write stay within that limit, but check how it looks on your profile.

faqs.q: Will it invent achievements?
faqs.a: No. It is told to use only what you provide and to leave out anything it cannot support.

faqs.q: Does it connect to my LinkedIn account?
faqs.a: No. You copy the text and paste it into LinkedIn yourself.

tools.name: React and Angular Code Playground
tools.title: Free React and Angular Code Playground
tools.description: Write React or Angular code in the editor and watch it run in a live preview. Practise interview exercises in your browser. Free account, nothing to install.
tools.h1: Free React and Angular code playground
tools.intro: Write React or Angular code in the editor and the live preview updates as you type, with the editor on the left and the preview on the right on wide screens. Start from an interview exercise such as a todo list, a cart or a login form, change it and see what happens. It runs in your browser, so nothing is installed and your code is not sent to our server.
steps: Choose React or Angular, then pick a starter exercise or clear the editor and write your own.
Edit the code. The preview updates a moment after you stop typing.
Read the console and any error message under the preview, fix the code, and copy it when you are happy.
tools.note: Your code runs in a sandboxed frame in your own browser and is not saved or sent to our server. It is for practice: it is not a full project setup, so there is no routing between files, no npm packages beyond the ones listed, and no network access guarantees.

faqs.q: Is my code saved or uploaded?
faqs.a: No. It is compiled and run in your browser inside a sandboxed frame. The editor keeps a copy in your own browser so a refresh does not lose it, and you can reset it any time.

faqs.q: Which versions and libraries are available?
faqs.a: React 19 with its hooks. For Angular, version 20 with core, common, forms, platform-browser and RxJS. Other npm packages are not available here.

faqs.q: Why does my Angular code with input() or constructor injection not work?
faqs.a: This playground runs Angular in the browser's JIT mode. It does not support the signal-based input(), output() and model() functions, or constructor injection by type. Use the @Input() and @Output() decorators and the inject() function instead. Signals, computed, effect, @if and @for work normally.

faqs.q: Can I use this for interview preparation?
faqs.a: Yes. It includes starter versions of common coding exercises. Always try writing the solution yourself first, then compare it with the model answers in the interview questions bank.

tools.name: Timed Interview Round
tools.title: Free Timed Interview Practice Round
tools.description: Practise interview questions against a countdown. Pick a topic, answer in your own words, reveal the model answer and rate yourself. Free account, no AI, nothing is saved.
tools.intro: Real interviews have a clock. Choose a topic, a level, how many questions and how long you get for each one. Answer in your own words or aloud before the time runs out, then read the model answer and rate yourself. Questions come from our interview question bank, so there is no AI and no daily limit.
steps: Choose a topic, a level, the number of questions and the time for each answer.
Answer before the timer ends, in notes or aloud. When it ends the model answer opens.
Rate yourself, finish the round and open the questions you want to review.
tools.note: Your notes stay on this screen and are not saved or sent. The rating is your own judgement, not a score from us. Model answers are one good way to answer, not the only one, and we cannot know what any particular employer will ask.

faqs.q: Does this use AI?
faqs.a: No. Questions and model answers come from our interview question bank. You judge your own answer by comparing it with the model answer.

faqs.q: Are these the questions I will be asked?
faqs.a: We cannot know what any employer will ask. The bank covers common, current topics, and the practice helps you explain things clearly under time pressure.

faqs.q: Is anything saved?
faqs.a: No. Your notes and ratings exist only on the page while you use it. Close the page and they are gone.

faqs.q: Where can I get written feedback on my answer?
faqs.a: The Mock Interview Practice tool gives written feedback against a model answer, using AI and a daily limit.

tools.name: Swift Code Reader
tools.title: Free Swift Code Reading Practice: Predict the Output
tools.description: Read short Swift snippets and predict what they print. Practise optionals, structs and classes, closures, defer, errors and more, with a clear explanation for each answer. Free account.
tools.h1: Swift code reading practice: predict the output
tools.intro: Reading code is a skill that interviews test. Each question shows a short Swift snippet. Pick what it prints, then read why. Topics include let and var, optionals, structs versus classes, closures, collections, defer and error handling. Real Swift cannot run in a browser, so this tool never runs code: you can confirm any answer in Xcode or a Swift Playground.
steps: Read the snippet and decide what it prints before you look at the choices.
Pick an answer and read the explanation, whether you were right or wrong.
Finish the set, then try a new one. Run any snippet in Xcode to confirm.
tools.note: The snippets are short and use only the Swift standard library. Each answer was worked out by hand, not by running the code here. If you think an answer is wrong, run it in Xcode and tell us through the contact page.

faqs.q: Why does the tool not run my Swift code?
faqs.a: Swift needs Apple's compiler and tools, which do not run in a web browser. To keep the tool honest, it asks you to predict the output and explains each answer instead of pretending to run code.

faqs.q: Where can I learn Swift from the start?
faqs.a: Our free iOS development course teaches Swift and SwiftUI step by step, and the advanced course goes further.

faqs.q: Do I need a Mac?
faqs.a: Not for this tool. To build real iPhone apps you need a Mac with Xcode.
